text: Three hours and forty-two minutes. On a single breath.
That's the longest dive ever recorded for any mammal — and the deepest belongs to the same kind of whale.
Not the sperm whale. It hunts giant squid more than two kilometres down, and it still loses.
This is Cuvier's beaked whale. Scientists off California tracked one to two thousand nine hundred and ninety-two metres.
The best scuba diver in history stopped at three hundred and thirty-two. This whale goes nine times deeper.
Under about three hundred times the pressure you're feeling right now.
So how does it survive? By doing something to its own lungs that sounds like a catastrophe.
How it pulls that off is level seven of the full dive, linked right here.
